guards.name: clock-single-source
guards.invariant: All rebuild wall-clock and monotonic-time reads route through the sole clock adapter, including aliased, imported, destructured, computed, and globalThis forms.

guards.name: dashboard-wire-boundary
guards.invariant: Ref frontend-backend-integration §8.2/§8.3/§8.13 and ref operator-trust §7: src/dashboard declares no handwritten structural mirror of a *Wire contract (schema-inferred types only), no dashboard file carries a registered workflow-id string literal — workflow identity reaches surfaces only as served data or the bundle-safe descriptor tuple, never as a branchable literal — and the bundled-import closure of EVERY *.html entry under src/dashboard reaches no Node built-in, so a shared domain contract can never drag node:path/node:fs/node:crypto into a browser bundle. 2i-F/D175 generalised that arm from the single hardcoded index.html to every entry, and added the phone-scope arm: the capture.html entry's closure may not reach src/dashboard/surfaces/**, src/dashboard/client/** or src/dashboard/app/**, because the capture ingress is ref operator-trust §7's ONE exception to loopback-only and serves that page's own asset closure — a single transitive import would ship the run detail, the command envelope and the SSE transport to a public origin without touching a route. Both arms carry negative controls: the config resolver's real node:crypto/node:path reach, and the operator entry's legitimate reach into all three forbidden roots.

guards.name: gate-coverage
guards.invariant: Preserve the reviewed gate-coverage architecture invariant.

guards.name: guard-manifest
guards.invariant: Every active architecture guard exists, is registered, and remains reachable from test:architecture.

guards.name: legacy-capability-disposition
guards.invariant: Every D58 legacy capability surface is classified exactly once by a recursively strict disposition union that has no proxy arm; status is the disposition's projection in both directions; every native/replaced target and every evidence token resolves to a real repo path, a real package.json script, or a real legacy path, and a decided entry must cite rebuild proof rather than only that legacy still exists; and no entry stays open on a milestone at or before the completedThrough the runtime itself reports (D184).

guards.name: legacy-change-accounting
guards.invariant: RETIRED by D150 (operator decision, 2026-08-05): the two repositories no longer touch each other in either direction, so there is nothing for an ongoing change-accounting ledger to reconcile. The guard required legacy's src/tests worktree to be CLEAN and every legacy commit since the Phase-0 baseline to be recorded here, which made an unrelated in-flight edit in the production repo a red gate in the rebuild. WHERE THE INVARIANT WENT: the risk it covered was a ported selector or page-state fact going stale after legacy fixed it. That is now covered by LIVE RE-VERIFICATION at each workflow's migration, which the charter already makes mandatory and pre-authorized, and which is strictly stronger — a selector checked against the live system beats one diffed against legacy's copy of it. `legacy-selector-port-provenance` still pins all 406 keys to a FIXED legacy commit's blobs, so it is unaffected by legacy moving on. config/legacy-change-accounting.json is kept as the frozen historical record of what was reconciled through the split; nothing reads it.

guards.name: legacy-selector-port-provenance
guards.invariant: All 406 legacy selector keys are represented exactly once with recipe-free search intent, exact clean-commit source/catalog Git provenance, and a selector definition at the pinned source line; disjoint candidate:<system>/<proposal> ids remain unclassified and cannot collide with any catalog kind, while ported semantic ids require exact fixture/live evidence bindings.

guards.name: legacy-test-disposition
guards.invariant: Every legacy test directory is classified exactly once and later-retirement candidates carry rebuild evidence. Owner re-pointed 2026-08-20: the design input this named (history/design-inputs/2026-07-27-testing-system-plan.md) is a historical memo, and D91 folded its coverage/sizing/preservation policy into ref guards-and-tests §3.14, which is where the rule now lives.

guards.name: manual-clock-test-only
guards.invariant: manualClock references, imports, re-exports, calls, and dynamic property access remain test-only.

guards.name: migration-history-immutability
guards.invariant: Every released SQLite authority migration version and ordered statement byte sequence is SHA-256 pinned; new schema work appends a new version and digest without editing, inserting into, deleting from, or reordering prior history.

guards.name: config-snapshot-generations
guards.invariant: The durable config leaf set is SHA-256 pinned per generation: adding or tightening a required config leaf without registering it in CONFIG_SNAPSHOT_GENERATIONS and bumping CURRENT_CONFIG_SNAPSHOT_GENERATION fails here, and a stored snapshot tolerates exactly the registered post-baseline leaves being absent — every other missing leaf, missing group, or unknown key still fails loud rather than being defaulted.

guards.name: no-secret-values-in-logs
guards.invariant: No rebuild template interpolation or diagnostic-sink argument carries a credential-named binding; only structurally named descriptors (name/id/path/file/family/env) and loop variables drawn from descriptor collections are permitted.

guards.name: operational-isolation
guards.invariant: Both runtimes on this machine bind distinct commands, state/artifact roots, ports, process locks, and browser profiles/sessions; the rebuild's isolation values come from one exported direct-const defineRuntimeIsolation call that a composition root invokes at top level through unshadowed named imports.

guards.name: parity-reference-authority
guards.invariant: D132: the ref frontend-backend-integration §7 parity lane can fail. Stored .a11y.yml/.meta.json references are compared, never rewritten, on a normal run — an accessibility-only change fails with a diff naming the reference and leaves the file untouched; refreshing requires PARITY_UPDATE=1 (npm run test:parity:update), the same single switch that drives Playwright's updateSnapshots so the pixel and semantic halves of a pair can never be refreshed independently. The served dist/dashboard must carry a build stamp binding both the working-tree source digest and the emitted output digest; a stale, unstamped, or post-build-edited bundle is refused before a port is bound. D145: the pixel half allows ZERO moved pixels (maxDiffPixels: 0) and pins its per-pixel colour tolerance explicitly — the old maxDiffPixelRatio: 0.001 was uncalibrated, hid a 112-px visible content change, and because updateSnapshots: "changed" reuses the same comparison it also stopped test:parity:update from repairing eight pairs whose .a11y.yml had refreshed while their .png stayed stale. No parity spec or helper may set its own screenshot allowance. All arms are executed against violating fixtures and through the lane's own captureA11yReference/startFixtureServer entry points.

guards.name: runtime-dependency-coverage
guards.invariant: The closed browser-system and vision-provider sets, their capabilities, endpoint preflight checks, secret families, and provider-model environment keys agree with the legacy inventory and with each other in both directions; the registry self-audit runs in the architecture lane.

guards.name: runtime-environment-coverage
guards.invariant: Every direct, computed, test-only, and documented environment read is explicitly classified; config and secret ownership remain bidirectionally complete.

guards.name: secrets-single-source
guards.invariant: Only src/domain/secrets.ts reads credential environment values; src/domain/config/** may read only statically resolved, non-credential CONFIG_ENV_BINDINGS keys, and every other rebuild module has zero environment access of any kind.

guards.name: strict-boundary-schemas
guards.invariant: Every cataloged external or durable boundary is schema-derived, recursively strict across object/union/lazy members, and rejects nested unknown keys and unsafe type/parser escape hatches.

guards.name: test-runtime-root-isolation
guards.invariant: No test may create, mutate, or delete a path rooted at a real runtime-isolation root (the isolation binding's state/artifact/lock/browser-profile properties, or a .auth*/.tracker* literal), directly or through a local binding; a test that constructs the real worker session factory must bind its own non-real paths.browserProfileRoot.

guards.name: ai-advisory-no-authority
guards.invariant: D178 (ref operator-trust §4.4): optional AI assistance reads the evidence and never becomes it. ZERO AUTHORITY EDGE — the advisory closure's VALUE-import graph (domain/trust/advisory, domain/dashboard/advisory, services/trust/advisory, infra/providers/gemini-advisory, server/dashboard/queries/advisory) may not reach any authority writer (the sqlite repositories, the command kernel, terminal authorization, the write sequencer/recovery, the receipt writer, run-failure, the diagnostic/knowledge/notification services, the ledger, the command services, either composition root, or control), and no command-family module (domain/commands, core/command-kernel, server/dashboard/commands/**) may import an advisory module — so an advisory value cannot cross into a command payload from either direction. A type-only import of a record SHAPE is deliberately not a path to that record's writer. The ONE permitted durable neighbour is D112 provider admission, at the composition root only. DECLARED REDACTION — every leaf a maximal FailureRecord presents carries a declaration and every declaration is exercised by it (both directions), no declaration pairs a classification with a transform redaction.ts forbids, only `safe-diagnostic` may leave as a VALUE, and an undeclared leaf refuses BY NAME rather than being dropped. ADVICE SHAPE — the closed advice schema exposes exactly headline/explanation/checks/confidence and strictly refuses retryability, a remediation kind, a run reference or a command. ROUTE — the advisory is its own POST /api/v1/runs/:runId/advisory, is never a run-detail section (a section would spend a provider budget on panel open), and no command-service module reaches the advisory query. Every arm runs against a violating fixture as well as the real subject.

guards.name: archive-invariants
guards.invariant: D179 (charter §25 / ref dashboard-surfaces §10.2): the D80 archive is a durable, self-contained, insert-only record. The archived-run READ path may not value-reach the workflow registry anywhere in its import closure — checked over the closure rather than one file, and executed against a checked-in violating fixture that reaches `src/base/workflow.ts` two hops away through a re-export, so a walker that resolved nothing could not pass. `version_bump_applications`, `archived_runs` and `archive_relaunches` abort every UPDATE and DELETE in SQL, proved by raw statements against a real migrated database with the rows present (an empty table would pass by doing nothing). No archive module names a `ledger/` PATH, and the only ledger IMPORT any of them may carry is the read-only read-through the archived-detail query calls — a `ledgerPartitions` POINTER field is the opposite of a violation, and resolving one back to the line it names is what keeps the pointer honest. The read-through itself is checked to name no write primitive, because a “repair” there would rewrite the record of what was really filed. The archived record's `contentDigest` is a fixed point over its own content, a tampered record digests differently, and a canonical round trip reproduces it — without which the `archiveFingerprint` a relaunch cites would be decoration. The five behavioural clauses of the exit criterion are pinned in tests/unit/archive-model.test.ts. D223's frozen section payloads are bound to the record's own `archiveSchemaGeneration` in BOTH directions: a reader admits a generation-1 record (those bytes are on disk and nothing may back-fill them) and a WRITER may not produce one, so a build that could not freeze the sections cannot record its own failure as "this record predates them"; a generation-1 record's canonical bytes are proved to gain no `sections` key and to hash to the digest it was written with, which is why the generation bump needed no migration.

guards.name: artifact-effect-boundary
guards.invariant: Artifact references expose stable UUID identity plus immutable digest/size/media type and no root or path; the real writer accepts only a non-symlinked rebuild-isolated artifact root, writes one metadata+payload object via temp→file-fsync→atomic-rename→directory-fsync, recovers cleanly across injected boundaries, returns the same ref for byte-identical content, and keeps task/workflow implementations away from direct mutable filesystem primitives.

guards.name: atomic-write-outbox
guards.invariant: Phase 1c atomic authority commit updates the fenced intent and attempt and inserts one schema-valid ledger outbox plus one terminal-span/generic-outcome outbox in one outer authority transaction; injected failure after every storage step rolls back every change and leaves authority generation unchanged. Browser sequencing and projection remain deferred to Phase 1f.

guards.name: authority-target-no-fallback
guards.invariant: RETIRED by D188 (2j, 2026-08-09): the invariant is held, and held harder, by `storage-recovery`. WHERE THE INVARIANT WENT: `AuthorityDatabase.open` refuses an existing-but-empty file by name rather than replacing it, `inspectExistingReadOnly` refuses a schema that is not exactly the supported version, and `storage-recovery` executes the whole family — corrupt, truncated, newer-schema, foreign-key-invalid, invariant-invalid and record-invalid files all open DEGRADED READ-ONLY with a named cause and zero bytes written. D181 added the restore half over a real-shaped copied database. A separate guard could only re-assert what those arms already execute against real SQLite files.

guards.name: bounded-task-deadline
guards.invariant: Every task invocation in the Phase-1 interpreter runs under a mandatory, immutable, scheduler-armed abortable deadline (ref execution-and-sessions §5 item 5): taskDeadlineMs is a required dependency with no default, both invocation arms race the deadline controller, and a task that ignores its signal still lands terminal failed with the wedged session poison-closed.

guards.name: canonical-input-snapshot
guards.invariant: Every registered canonical-input schema is transform-free anywhere in its graph and round-trips its ingress samples; a corrupted snapshot fails loud instead of being re-derived from ingress; and a snapshot only crosses schema hashes through a checked-in, factory-sealed, acyclic migration chain.

guards.name: capture-durability-and-scope
guards.invariant: D174 (ref data-intake-and-edit-data §5.1; ref clock-config-secrets §capture ingress; ref operator-trust §7): the phone reaches capture and nothing else, and a capture bundle is durable before it is reported. SCOPE — the routes registered under /api/v1/capture/phone/ and the declared CAPTURE_PHONE_ROUTES union are the same set in BOTH directions; a `:param` matches exactly one segment so no path walks out of the prefix; no operator route or catch-all can be spelled as a phone route or served as a phone asset; and a request arriving on the configured ingress Host is refused with a status and body BYTE-IDENTICAL to an unrouted path, driven through a real Hono app with a no-ingress negative control proving the filter is what refuses. ENUMERATION — the raw token is never durable or wire state (only its domain-separated digest is), the session wire carries neither `token` nor `tokenDigest`, the strict record refuses a token field outright, and the credential rides a header rather than any path or query value. DURABILITY — only the command kernel, the authority database, the finalize projector and the capture service's two declared clock transitions (expiry, first-connect) may write `capture_sessions` or the finalization outbox; ONLY the finalize projector may declare a session `finalized`, so nothing can report "Sent" without the outbox having settled; and the record's own refinements (a finalized session names its bundle and enqueued handoff, a failed one names its failure handoff, a finalizing/failed one carries a generation, the D174 ingress stamp stays read-forward optional) are each proven by a violating fixture. Every arm runs against a violating fixture as well as the real subject.

guards.name: commit-routes-through-mutation
guards.invariant: RETIRED by D188 (2j, 2026-08-09): held by `task-driver-boundary`, which refuses a `commit` implementation outside a store driver owner that validates its capability AND refuses premature capability forgery, both against a checked-in violating fixture. WHERE THE INVARIANT WENT: the capability itself became runtime-unforgeable at D127 — a module-private WeakSet in `src/core/write-sequencer.ts` is the sole mint and drivers verify with `assertSequencerMintedMutationCapability` — so routing is enforced by construction and the guard only has to keep the allowlist honest.

guards.name: control-command-single-path
guards.invariant: D113: exactly one command kernel executes ref dashboard-surfaces's D95 command protocol — the journal, audit, and start-plan consumption are statically confined to it; every family/action dispatches to a typed result with Phase-1f active arms executing and every later arm rejected capability-unavailable with zero authority-generation advance; command ids replay byte-exactly; every run verb CASes the CALLER's expected version with no exceptions — presentation (D233 — a stale rename may not overwrite a current name) and bump (D233's rule applied, D234) included; typed gate results parse the descriptor's exact schema before storage; notification stays read/unread/snooze; capture targets cannot spell a run id; and an injected active-run lookup failure enqueues zero runs.

guards.name: delegation-manifest
guards.invariant: Delegation edge ids are unique per workflow; one D102 policy vocabulary spans builder, manifest, dependency row, and UI; the plan fingerprint covers edge, cardinality, join, policy, and every child id and input; a drifted replay fails loud; a join runs only over the complete outcome set; and a zero-child fan-out stays an explicit satisfied join with a writable durable manifest.

guards.name: descriptor-coverage
guards.invariant: Ref workflow-model §1.4: one table-driven sweep over DESCRIPTORS — unique ids/codes/icons, the module tuple agreeing with every derived registry in both directions, contract placement and examples, the derived browser-system union, concretely typed child-run targets, the bundle-safe value-import closure of every descriptor module, a current build manifest, and descriptor-to-impl pairing tracked explicitly rather than implicitly. The manifest is current in BOTH senses: the parsed manifest equals a fresh recomputation, and the checked-in module text equals the generator's exact bytes — formatting/ordering drift that deepEqual is structurally blind to fails the gate, proven by a negative control that reformats the module and shows the parsed arm stays green. The byte arm is one shared function used by the guard and by `npm run build:manifest:check`, whose presence in package.json is pinned so the `--check` CLI can never again ship wired to nothing. D107's pending-impl bindings are audited in both directions with a live fixture per staleness arm: an entry no descriptor uses, and (D184) an entry a store now implements.

guards.name: driver-lease-boundary
guards.invariant: Drivers exist only inside WorkerSessionManager.withDriver's callback lease: withDriver is consumed only by the graph interpreter, the browser-session factory's open() is invoked only inside worker-sessions, and only the worker loop constructs a WorkerSessionManager ownership scope.

guards.name: dry-run-composition-submit-free
guards.invariant: RETIRED by D188 (2j, 2026-08-09): held by `write-safety-contract` plus the executable scenario `kuali-timekeeper-annotation/dry-run-preview`, which runs the REAL write sequencer over a REAL authority database and asserts DURABLE absence — zero `write_intents`, zero `run_checkpoints`, zero `durable_outbox` rows — rather than inspecting a composition for the absence of a call. WHERE THE INVARIANT WENT: `executeDryRun` is a separate arm and `executeTransaction` with `dryRun` refuses loudly, so a submit-free dry run is a property of the kernel's shape, and the scenario is what proves it on rows.

guards.name: edit-data-field-policy
guards.invariant: Edit Data's default is read-only: a descriptor must declare every correctable node+field path, a declared path must resolve through the producing READ task node's own output schema (a transaction node's output is a write proof and never correctable), the negative controls run through the real descriptor factory, every registered descriptor's policy parses the closed schema, and the edit-checkpoint save command stays in the ACTIVE partition so a declared policy can never outrun the kernel arm whose CAS-against-resume-fence honours it (D166).

guards.name: evidence-receipt
guards.invariant: A terminal run's receipt is strict at every level and carries the graph/config/input fingerprints, a source and observation instant for every fact, a filed binding proof for every verified write, and one explicit confidence; `verified-done` is refused for non-verified confidence, an unresolved mandatory fact or obligation, any warning, or a failure id, each proven by a violating fixture. Redaction is DECLARED: every leaf of every registered canonical-input sample and every used contract's sealed example carries a classification whose transform its classification permits, an undeclared leaf fails loud rather than dropping, a declaration that disagrees with domain/secrets.ts fails, and no env key, cookie, storage-state, or raw-SSN canary reaches a built receipt. The diagnostic-bundle half of ref guards-and-tests §3.10 activates with the bundle capture slice. D199 — a receipt is bound to the surfaces its derivation CONSUMES, never to the descriptor's source closure: `descriptorFingerprint` is the closure the RUN executed under, read from its own envelope, so a settled receipt re-derives byte-identically after any edit that leaves every consumed surface intact, and a receipt that took the current build's `contractFingerprint` stranded every already-settled run on the next unrelated edit. Resolvability is a named check table — `workflow-identity`, `descriptor-version`, `canonical-input`, `evidence-graph`, `terminal-dependency-set`, `declared-evidence` — printed in full with both fingerprints, `[held]`/`[MOVED]`/`[skip]` distinct and no waiver arm. `declared-evidence` is the one check whose baseline is the stored receipt row, because the declared redaction and obligation tables live OUTSIDE every descriptor closure and can move with `contractFingerprint` byte-identical; the immutable insert stays underneath as the backstop. D204 — a GATE's durable evidence is a `gate_results` row and never a checkpoint, so a resolved gate node emits its payload's leaves as facts sourced `gate-result` (carrying authority's own `resolvedBy`/`resolvedAt`, never a payload claim), ONE `kind: "gate"` decision naming the approver, the instant, the resolving command and the bound evidence digest, and a `verified` obligation in place of the `unknown` a checkpoint-only derivation reported. The outcome is DECLARED per `(workflow, gate)` in `src/domain/trust/gate-decisions.ts` and never sniffed from a field name: every gate node of every registered descriptor has a declaration whose decision and bound-evidence leaves classify under a `gate-result` redaction scope, an undeclared gate and an unlisted arm value both fail loud, an orphan declaration or gate-scoped classification fails, and a foreign run's gate row, a gate that left the graph and an undeclared arm are executed as negative controls against the REAL gated descriptor, and the UNDECLARED `(workflow, gate)` pair — unreachable through the builder precisely because every registered gate node is declared — is pinned directly on `gateDecisionFor`, which is the only route from a stored row to a `DecisionEvidence.outcome`.

guards.name: fresh-session-boundary
guards.invariant: A browser-session boundary is authored or identity-forced, never inferred: the `fresh-boundary` close reason exists only inside the session-ownership modules, every task/workflow `session:` need is a string literal rather than a computed value, repeated reuse-worker needs mint no boundary, and both an authored session:"fresh" need and a D116 (worker,system,resolvedInstance,configFingerprint) reuse-identity mismatch close the old resource with an accepted page/context proof BEFORE the replacement opens and authenticates. The descriptor-level node-execution ordering arm lands with the first workflow that authors a fresh-boundary node.

guards.name: identity-gate-before-commit
guards.invariant: Ref write-safety §14.6 #2: in a separation-class descriptor BOTH sinks — every transaction node and the terminal result — are graph-reachable only through an operator gate. Every dependsOn ancestry path from a sink must reach the gate's own ancestry (the gate plus its transitive dependsOn closure) before a graph root; a node OUTSIDE that ancestry is data the operator never saw at the gate, and a side read feeding the sink is the violation. The terminal arm landed with separations chunk 3 because a read-only chunk produces an APPROVED SUBJECT a later composition binds a write's expected side to, so a terminal result reachable without the gate hands that composition an unconfirmed identity. The registered gate is additionally pinned to ref write-safety §14.4's IdentityApprovalResult schema hash — the exact value executeResolveGate compares an incoming payload against — so §14.6 risk 5 (a gate result becoming free-form control state) is structurally closed. Executed both ways against gated and ungated fixtures, including a synthesized side read.

guards.name: knowledge-fix-integrity
guards.invariant: D139 (ref operator-trust §4, §9): knowledge records carry status/scope/evidence/validity and forward supersession refs, and admission is audited INSIDE the insert transaction because an insert-only table cannot retract a duplicate. Two active records may not claim the same scoped rule — same scope plus same normalized title or a shared regression scenario — without the successor explicitly superseding the predecessor; a supersedes ref that names nothing recorded, a self-reference, and a duplicate id are each refused with the conflict named. The generated per-system KNOWLEDGE.md is the active view alone: superseded, retired, and unverified records never reach it. A verified FixRecord requires a commit plus non-empty verification evidence and a regression scenario, a draft may claim neither, and a verified fix may not link knowledge that is missing or itself unverified. A raw chronological lesson append is not authority: triageLesson has exactly one arm and it returns the obligations still owed, never a record.

guards.name: ledger-projector
guards.invariant: D134 (ref write-safety §6): the ledger is projected by ONE serialized, actor-attributed writer and is never pruned. No module outside src/infra/ledger/ may append the ledger, and no module that can name ledger/ may call a deletion primitive — both arms run against violating fixtures, and pruneEventStreams stays structurally blind to the ledger (EVENT_STREAMS is exactly spans+notes). A line's bytes and digest are a pure function of (outbox payload, seq) with a versioned domain separator, and its partition comes from the entry's own confirmedAt in UTC, never from wall-clock now. Sequence assignment is idempotent by outboxId, burns no sequence on repeat, refuses a conflicting line digest, and refuses any projector that does not hold the exact (system,date) lease generation. A non-dense partition sequence degrades the store read-only at boot, and the projection report's degraded arm is a closed reason set that no projected arm can smuggle.

guards.name: legacy-preservation
guards.invariant: D93: the path->whole-file-SHA preservation manifest existed to decide which legacy files the same-tree scan treated strictly. With the scan retired the manifest has no consumer; legacy files are governed by the legacy repo's own gates, and its baseline file set is now read directly from git by legacy-change-accounting.

guards.name: multi-worker-overlap
guards.invariant: ACTIVATED BY D182 (ref execution-and-sessions §7.1 rows C1-C4). More than one REAL `runWorkerLoop` instance, with distinct worker ids, races ONE workflow queue over ONE shared authority database, and the durable claim set is sampled at every span event and every driver call rather than read once at the end. Two facts hold at once and pull in opposite directions: no worker EVER owns two rows in `claimed|validating|running` (ref execution-and-sessions §0.3, sampled live so a double claim released before the end could not hide), and the fleet genuinely overlaps -- the observed maximum of workers holding work simultaneously equals the worker count, which is ref execution-and-sessions §7's 'parallelism silently serializes' risk stated as a measurement. Every enqueued run is executed exactly once, claimed by exactly one worker, and ends terminal `done` at claim generation 1 and attempt 1, so a second claim or a requeue is visible in authority rather than only in a report. A row held by a live loop is never served to a sibling `claimNext` and the holder's own second `claimNext` throws by name. A sweep interleaved with a live heartbeat requeues only the genuinely stale row -- the freshly renewed claim keeps its owner, generation and attempt -- and the requeued row is proved re-claimable by the same live loop. A zombie heartbeat whose row was swept and re-owned reports `lost` and abandons instead of stamping a heartbeat over the new owner.

guards.name: no-positional-identity
guards.invariant: No durable identity is positional or borrowed: every run, worker, workflow, node, gate, actor, delegation-edge, and extracted-record id rejects an index, an ordinal, and a stringified number, and a UUID cannot be spelled as any slug-shaped id, so a run id can never stand in as a worker id.

guards.name: notification-durability
guards.invariant: D138 (ref dashboard-surfaces §2.6/§10.4 D79b; ref operator-trust §6): a notification is a durable record FIRST and a desktop delivery second. `publish` settles create-or-fold in one authority transaction and only then attempts OS delivery, and the load-bearing arm injects a delivery that throws — the item must still be durably unread with its count and version untouched, because the operator who missed the toast has only the inbox left. No per-attempt delivery state is written. Each of ref dashboard-surfaces §2.6's closed triggers commits an item and routes to its ratified D79b channel (failed/gate-waiting/write-parked/repeating/storage → ping, verified-done → inbox), each carries its own dedupe identity that excludes the occurrence, and a repeat FOLDS into the one (actorId, dedupeFingerprint) row — count up, lastSeenAt advanced, unread again — rather than minting a second. Snooze suppresses delivery only and never flips status; read state and snooze move independently; a stale version is refused. The trigger event union is ids, closed codes, and counts, so notification text has no free-text channel a captured value could enter through.

guards.name: one-projection-counts
guards.invariant: D81 (ref dashboard-surfaces §10.1): there is exactly ONE server-side run/queue projection and every dashboard count descends from its payload. Structurally, the count fields (monthCounts/workflowCounts/statusCounts) are constructed in exactly one production module — src/server/dashboard/projectors/run-queue-projection.ts — and nowhere else in src/, so a second aggregate endpoint or a client-side re-derivation fails by file name. A seeded world with delegated (operation+member), rejected/failed, gated, terminal and ARCHIVED rows proves Workflow Panel total == Status Bar sum == rendered Queue Panel row count by construction, with containment and the D179 archive exclusion applied once inside the projection (D234 retired the hidden-row exclusion, leaving archiving as the only whole-run one). D236 adds the ONE ratified exemption and BOUNDS it from both sides: the Activity report's write-ledger block is a different authority — append-only, never pruned, never archived, so its entries outlive the runs that filed them — reported beside the totals and never reconciled against them, and the guard pins that a block is BUILT only in src/domain/dashboard/activity.ts + src/infra/ledger/ledger-read-through.ts and ASKED FOR only in the read-through + the one projection, by exact set equality both ways, so a third counting path over the ledger fails by file name. The behavioural half files real ledger lines into the seeded world and requires the block to move while every count stays byte-identical: 'reported beside the totals' is a claim about what does not happen.

guards.name: one-time-import-offline
guards.invariant: PLANNED, re-owned by D188 (2j, 2026-08-09) from the meaningless `phase-1-or-later` to the cutover gate. The invariant is that the one-time import of legacy operational data runs OFFLINE against a copy and never reaches a live system. It has no subject yet: no import path exists in this tree, and D150/D156 retired the legacy accounting that would have fed one. It activates in the commit that builds the cutover data migration (doc 05 §Exit criteria), not before.

guards.name: permanent-key-dedupe
guards.invariant: A strict system-scoped natural idempotency key and its derived digest identify one permanent SQLite intent across sequential and independent competing connections; committed and observed-present rows cannot be reopened, observed-present creates no attempt or write ledger/span outbox, and any key/digest mismatch fails loud.

guards.name: ucpath-person-org-strict
guards.invariant: The UCPath Person Organizational Summary runtime pins exact legacy provenance while rejecting body-name scans, observed-EID overwrite, extraction-error empty defaults, missing-grid not-found inference, swallowed clears, and drill-null fallbacks; search results expand before extraction and again after Return to Search, Employment Instances expand before assignment selection, enabled View All must transition to View N while disabled View All alone proves already-complete, contextual one-to-many selector ports remain closed and unique, every operation locator resolves through dual evidence, and both subject proofs fail loud. The locator-coverage arm is scoped to the two Person Org SCREENS in both directions (D130 added a second UCPath screen family), and the SS Smart HR receipt elements are asserted present and unreachable from this operation so the scoping can never go vacuous.

guards.name: preflight-coverage
guards.invariant: PLANNED, re-owned by D188 (2j, 2026-08-09). Its subject is the PREFLIGHT FRAMEWORK's own coverage — that every declared runtime dependency has a preflight scenario exercising its failure, not merely its presence. `runtime-dependency-coverage` and `runtime-environment-coverage` already hold the declaration side, and `authority.health` is the one runner wired end to end; the missing half is a corpus of executed fault scenarios (`src/domain/trust/preflight-scenarios.ts` declares them, nothing runs them). It activates with the first migration that adds a preflight runner, which is where the second declared fault gets a producer.

guards.name: provider-capability-boundary
guards.invariant: Every capability maps exactly once to a strict immutable provider budget and reaches remote I/O only through the single durable admission kernel; whole-src and transitive task import scans confine raw network/vendor modules and adapters to infra/providers, forbid hidden ProviderClient construction, prove exhaustion makes zero adapter calls/non-sleep requeue, and keep the adapter surface deliberate: infra/providers holds the deterministic harness plus the reviewed production adapters (D161's gemini ocr.extract first), the run executor is the ONE production consumer (D162: per-invocation admitted clients over the run's retained config snapshot, ingredients composed by the worker root), and production pools stay absent until 2h-D. The same single-owner rule covers the frontend transport, ONE owner per browser bundle: src/dashboard/client/** for the operator bundle and the single file src/dashboard/phone/capture-client.ts for the phone bundle (2i-F/D175) — named as one file rather than a subtree, so a phone component that reached for fetch directly still fails. D184 adds the allowlist-hygiene half: every name in the three D162/D178 allowlists must resolve to a git-visible module (one dead entry, the admission module listed as its own importer, is deleted), and the D68 declared provider inventory is reconciled with the built adapter tree in both directions — every ProviderId has EITHER a reviewed adapter-module list that exists OR a reviewed declared-without-adapter reason, so the four key-only providers (groq/mistral/openrouter/sambanova) are a recorded state rather than a silent divergence.

guards.name: rebuild-gates
guards.invariant: D93: the absent-tree / present-but-empty temp_src activation dance retires with temp_src. This repo's roots exist from its first commit; gate-coverage pins the plain script family and guard-manifest still proves every active arm resolves a non-empty file set.

guards.name: recovery-negative-proof-settlement
guards.invariant: Retry authority requires the exact configured number of schema-valid post-window observations at or beyond both injected-Clock timing boundaries, all bound to the fenced key and exact authoritative query/source/source-state; early, single, malformed, future, inconsistent, wrong-boundary, ambiguous, unknown, present, and operator-only evidence never becomes retryable.

guards.name: runtime-isolation
guards.invariant: D93: two repositories share no module graph, so the cross-tree bridge scan proves an impossibility. The configuration half — distinct commands, state/artifact roots, ports, process locks, and browser profiles on one machine — survives in operational-isolation.

guards.name: scenario-coverage
guards.invariant: Every branch arm, gate open/resolve, delegation size/replay/policy, and transaction outcome derived from the node tuple is claimed by a registered scenario, and every claim resolves to a path that still exists — so a renamed arm cannot keep a deleted path looking covered. D185 adds the corpus DIRECTORY, which the registered-set audits structurally cannot see: `tests/scenario/` holds exactly two declared kinds — a graph scenario (`*.scenario.test.ts`) and an integration walk (`*.walk.test.ts`) — and every file on disk is one of them. An `it` title whose head parses as a ScenarioId is a CLAIM, so a typo stays a claim and fails rather than being reclassified as prose, and every claim must be a manifest row naming THAT file or a graph-claim corpus id; every manifest row must name a file the corpus contains and a test that file declares; a graph scenario that claims nothing, a walk that claims a graph path or carries a manifest row, and a file of neither kind are each refused by name. `auditScenarioCorpusLayout` is pure over an injected listing, and every arm carries a negative control built by moving exactly one thing in the REAL corpus.

guards.name: semantic-ui-registry
guards.invariant: Every server-private semantic UI definition has a globally unique classified id, collision-free search intent, resolved same-system/same-screen acyclic dependencies, non-vacuous globally unique verification scenarios, exact dual sanitized evidence-to-screen/scenario/date/port-row bindings, and byte-fresh recipe-free generated catalogs; disjoint legacy candidate ids cannot enter any runtime catalog kind. The guarded projection set is DERIVED, never enumerated: it equals the set of stores shipping a `driver/ui-registry.ts` in both directions (no unguarded publisher, no orphan UI-CATALOG.md), so a newly added store's markdown cannot escape freshness enforcement the way `src/stores/kuali/UI-CATALOG.md` did. Every derived projection — the JSON and each per-system markdown — carries stale and missing negative controls through an injected reader.

guards.name: single-flight-login
guards.invariant: Session login is single-flight within one worker/system session creation (ref execution-and-sessions §4): store.session.login is invoked only inside the worker session manager, and two concurrent leases for one system produce exactly one session open and one authentication.

guards.name: sleep-budget
guards.invariant: RETIRED by D188 (2j, 2026-08-09): ref execution-and-sessions §7's row reads "wait-for-timeout ratchet + span sleep budget", and both halves are now enforced elsewhere. WHERE THE INVARIANT WENT: the `wait-for-timeout-allowlist` ratchet bans `waitForTimeout` outright, and every wait in the kernel goes through the injected `MonotonicDeadlineScheduler` with `bounded-task-deadline` holding the per-invocation bound — so there is no authored sleep for a budget to measure. D182's soak runs 3 workers x 30 runs with a manual clock and a manual scheduler and never advances a real timer, which is the same fact executed.

guards.name: storage-recovery
guards.invariant: Native online backups self-verify the completed copy, bind immutable manifests to final bytes, coalesce generation-follow-up work, fail closed into read-only degraded authority, keep doctor read-only, and permit only stopped-proof offline restore from an exact verified compatible backup without exposing DatabaseSync or using live-WAL copy/VACUUM fallbacks.

guards.name: subject-before-fence
guards.invariant: Every transaction pairs compatible prepare/commit subject declarations observed after prepare in one system; the live sequencer orders prepare-end < fresh subject observation < fence-commit < mutation-call on one lease; mismatch/unknown/missing observation produces zero fence and zero click with a poisoned page; alternating EIDs through one pooled page bind distinct digests; every minted MutationCapability is bound to the exact fenced WriteBindingProof digest and is refused by the production Kuali driver when it was not sequencer-minted; unscoped commits require a reviewed allowlisted reason, fail-both-ways.

guards.name: task-contract-sealing
guards.invariant: Read, prepare, and commit contracts are minted only by the validating deep-seal factory; the exact effect-discriminated runtime definition rejects unknown/effect-only fields, empty error-code lists, and non-memory prepare checkpoints; recursive schemas reject nested open/any/unknown/record escapes; parsed canonical examples and closed write-safety proofs agree; unscoped commits require reviewed reason ids; schema-owned paths/tiers/references fail loud; inferred error codes stay literal; and an AST plus transitive import graph protects every src/**/contracts/** module from runtime imports, forged seals, casts, and dynamic-import bypasses.

guards.name: task-driver-boundary
guards.invariant: AST and transitive import-graph audits confine static/dynamic Playwright access, raw browser types, locator/frame/getBy/newPage/evaluate/$ operations, and private driver/session ownership to the two raw-browser owner families — per-system driver/session modules and the `src/infra/browser/**` worker session factory that owns concrete browser creation; task/workflow code consumes typed semantic ids and proofs and may reach neither family transitively. MutationCapability may be conjured by `as`/`satisfies` nowhere outside `src/base/mutation-capability.ts`, `mintMutationCapability` has exactly one permitted caller (`src/core/write-sequencer.ts`), and a `commit` implementation is legal only inside a `src/stores/<system>/driver/**` owner that validates its capability before clicking (D122).

guards.name: task-store-boundaries
guards.invariant: All nine closed browser systems have exactly one declared store and fail-loud unwired session provider; driver/session/store systems match, OnBase alone is identity-exclusive, typed task bindings enforce effect/access/session/provider boundaries, and the registry exact-matches implementations to the contract corpus while resolving every scenario/probe/verifier reference.

guards.name: transaction-pairing
guards.invariant: A transaction pairs prepare and commit arms from one system under one lease, binds the commit key from workflow input and declared upstream outputs only, declares a positive probe-to-fence budget and a dry-run policy, carries a same-system read probe, and no commit contract is reachable as a standalone step anywhere in src/.

guards.name: worker-teardown-soak
guards.invariant: ACTIVATED BY D182 (ref execution-and-sessions §7.1 rows C5-C8). Ref execution-and-sessions §7's first mechanical-guard row -- 'worker-soak test asserts max active claims per worker is exactly 1' -- named a test that did not exist; this is it, plus the teardown half. The soak drains 30 queued runs across 3 real `runWorkerLoop` instances over ONE authority database on a manual clock and a manual scheduler (no real timer participates), then proves authority intact rather than merely counting outcomes: every run terminal `done` exactly once at claim generation 1 and attempt 1, no row left in `claimed|validating|running`, exactly one `run_terminal_outbox` row per run, zero unresolved write intents, zero pending ledger outbox, and `AuthorityDatabase.inspectExistingReadOnly` re-reading the file so its ~30 named SQL invariants, quick_check and foreign-key scan all pass -- a soak that corrupted the claim index would still count 30 done runs. The ledger projector is asked and must AGREE there is nothing to project. Teardown: a stop signal mid-run abandons rather than terminalizing over a claim it can no longer prove, the interrupted lease is closed as `poisoned` (never as a clean worker-stop), the row is LEFT under its now-stale claim, and ref execution-and-sessions §3's recovery sweep -- not the dying loop -- is what requeues it for a successor that drains it to `done`; `closeAll("worker-stop")` closes nothing while a driver callback is in flight, refuses a SECOND concurrent `closeAll` by name, and refuses every new lease once teardown began; and an operation failure whose poison-close cannot prove closure raises one AggregateError naming BOTH, retains the resource as poisoned, refuses reuse, and still names every failing system when worker-stop aggregates.

guards.name: workflow-editor-compile-integrity
guards.invariant: ACTIVATED AT PHASE A ONLY (D176, 2i-G). Ref guards-and-tests §3.10's first sentence — 'read-only explorer projections round-trip from the real descriptor/contract/UI registries' — is enforced over the REAL registry, not a fixture, in both directions: the served workflow list equals WORKFLOW_MODULES in its own order; each workflow's node identities, order, kinds and dependsOn equal descriptorRuntimeNodes(descriptor); the rendered task ids equal workflowProjections(descriptor).contracts exactly; every derived graph coverage point is rendered exactly once; every UI id named resolves in buildSafeUiCatalog() AND equals that catalog's own taskUses for the contract; every printed source link RESOLVES and names a git-tracked file; and no edge names a node the graph does not carry. Two static arms keep it derivable rather than copyable: the projection must read through descriptorRuntimeNodes/workflowProjections and may carry no literal node list, and neither the projection, the wire, nor either surface may hardcode a registered workflow id. Phase A's read-only boundary is structural: neither surface may reach /api/v1/commands, call the command client, or issue a non-GET request; both routes are registered app.get with no POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE counterpart; and the catalog query freshness-asserts the COMMITTED artifact while naming no writer (the 2026-08-03 tracked-artifact lesson). D79a's trim is pinned too: no descriptor.generated.ts exists anywhere, every registered workflow has a source-authored descriptor.ts + module.ts, and config/workflow-design/ carries no runtime authority. NOT YET ENFORCED — ref operator-trust §5.3/§5.4's Phase B: the closed presentation/policy draft union, stale-base apply refusal, and the code-change brief. None of that exists (there is no draft, validate, or apply), so this guard gains those arms in the same commit that builds them. Each static arm runs against a violating fixture.

guards.name: explorer-prose-declared
guards.invariant: D229 — every REGISTERED workflow serves the descriptor's own `summary` and every node its own `purpose`, asserted over the REAL composition root through `buildWorkflowExplorer`, with each served sentence compared byte-for-byte against the descriptor's declaration so the projection cannot compose one from a label or a contract title. The wire carries an `absent` arm rather than throwing — the explorer serves every workflow in ONE document, so refusing the whole surface over a missing sentence would take the operator's index of the system down for a piece of prose — and this guard is what makes that arm unreachable in the product. Three negative controls run through `defineWorkflowDescriptor` itself: a partial node-purpose list, a purpose naming an undeclared node, and a node named twice are each refused by name; a descriptor declaring nothing is accepted, which is the arm a fixture graph legitimately takes. A fixture descriptor is deliberately out of scope — it is not in the composition root, and prose about a graph nobody runs is prose nobody reads.

guards.name: wire-connectivity
guards.invariant: Ref frontend-backend-integration §8.8 ("every advertised section has a query"), generalised to the whole wire and enforced in BOTH directions against config/pending-wire-bindings.json — D107's pending-impl-bindings pattern one layer up. FOUR joints: (1) every literal arm of RunDetailSectionResponseSchema, read by walking the zod union at RUNTIME rather than by regex, is either returnable by availableSections — proven by CALLING it over RunRecordSchema-parsed records covering every RunStateSchema member and every RunOutcomeSchema member, with and without the optional trust seam — or declared in the manifest; (2) every ActionCommandKeySchema verb is accepted by CommandRequestSchema, every kernel verb is either serveable as an action or named in a closed KERNEL_ONLY_COMMANDS table with the reason it targets something other than a run row, and — the third direction, added by D234 — every serveable verb is one some PRODUCER emits, read by CALLING queueRowActions over every QueueStatusSchema member in both member and non-member shapes and by scanning the comment-stripped descriptor literals of src/server/dashboard/queries/run-detail.ts, so a key the vocabulary names and nothing projects (unhide, for a whole phase) FAILS; (3) every /api or /events path referenced under src/dashboard/client/** and src/dashboard/phone/capture-client.ts resolves to a route app.<method>("…") registers in src/server/dashboard/routes/api.ts, with interpolations reduced to opaque segments and query/fragment dropped. The reverse arms are what keep the manifest honest (D184/D188): a declared arm that has become reachable, a declared arm the schema no longer carries, a declared route a client now calls, and a declared route nobody serves each FAIL. The lifecycle sweep asserts it covered every RunStateSchema member, so a new state fails here until somebody decides what it serves. Negative controls run through the same entry points: a synthesized orphan arm, a verb the kernel must never accept (force-done), a key named only in a comment (which must not count as projected), the retired unhide and the never-existing force-done both absent from the projected set, an unserved client path, and four route-matcher over-match cases. (4) Every WIRE MIRROR of a durable vocabulary is member-for-member identical to its original, compared through z.toJSONSchema rather than a hand-listed member set — src/domain/dashboard/run-detail.ts re-declares ref write-safety's parked-write codes and SubjectEvidenceSchema, and src/domain/dashboard/projection.ts re-declares RunPrioritySchema, because those originals reach node:crypto or the checkpoint closure and these modules are in the dashboard bundle's reach (ref frontend-backend-integration §8.13). A mirror is the one joint with no import to keep it honest, so a member added to either side, a regex loosened on one, or a branded id swapped for a bare string has to fail here or nowhere.

guards.name: write-safety-contract
guards.invariant: Every effect:commit contract declares complete write safety with no escape hatch: nontrivial proofSchema, normal-output/present-probe extractors, outputFromProof reconstruction, and a same-store read probe; the completion union admits receipt AND save-verify/upload-verify without a confirmation number; and ref write-safety SS4 recovery routes probe-first with present proof schema-validated before backfill, single early absence yielding zero retry authority, only D64/D69 stabilized evidence settling retryable, indeterminate arms parking, and the permanent key blocking every second fence.

guards.name: authentication-proof-not-url
guards.invariant: Ref execution-and-sessions §4: a browser session's authentication is never concluded from a URL. Every store login recipe is built by defineVerifiedLoginRecipe so its content-level proof runs on EVERY return path, no recipe produces a LoginResult outside that wrapper, every landed BrowserSystemBinding supplies a verifier rather than an isAuthenticatedUrl predicate, and the factory's neutral reset asserts through assertAuthenticatedApplication.

guards.name: intake-canonical-field-registry
guards.invariant: Ref data-intake-and-edit-data §1's canonical field vocabulary is frozen against the recorded D58/D68 scan in config/canonical-field-inventory.json, and the coverage is checked in BOTH directions: a canonical field no scanned source evidences is unevidenced vocabulary, and a scanned legacy field with no disposition is the silent omission ref data-intake-and-edit-data §1 forbids. Every scanned field must still appear in the legacy file the scan names, so the frozen legacy tree doubles as a drift detector. Each registry entry must hold together: its declared (classification, redactTransform) pair is one ref clock-config-secrets permits, a deferred shape carries an auditNote and a resolved one does not, and no normalized header alias claims two fields — an ambiguous alias would make the §2.5 scorer's top hit arbitrary. The definition factory additionally refuses any example its own coerce+parse rejects. Every arm runs against a violating fixture.

guards.name: intake-mapping-boundary
guards.invariant: Ref data-intake-and-edit-data §7 vectors #1/#3/#6/#13. The §2.5 suggestion scorer proposes and structurally cannot bind: `suggestions.ts` may not name `confirmedAt` nor reach the binding schemas, and `ColumnBindingSchema.parse` appears in exactly one file — `confirmBinding` in src/domain/intake/mapping.ts, which additionally refuses a target the projection does not declare and a column not present in the file. A saved binding re-resolves by normalized header plus occurrence ONLY: a bound column that is absent reverts to unbound and loud, and the stored index — kept solely to report that a column moved — never rescues it. `defineIntakeProjection` requires each target path to resolve to the canonical field's exact schema OBJECT (a structurally identical copy is refused) while keeping two targets that share one canonical concept independently bindable. The whole src/domain/intake tree stays free of Node built-ins because the mapping grid is a browser surface (ref frontend-backend-integration §8.13). Every static arm runs against a violating fixture, plus a comment-only fixture that must NOT fire.

guards.name: ocr-producer-parity
guards.invariant: D151: every OCR producer — the provider pipeline, an AI the operator runs in their own terminal, or the operator — is held to the same rules structurally, not merely in tests. `admitOcrExtraction` may not BRANCH on `source` (no `source.kind ===`, no switch on it); copying the source onto the record is fine, testing it is not, because one `if` is all it takes for "the provider path is trusted" to creep in where no sample-input test would necessarily catch it. Only the gate may parse an `AdmittedExtraction`, so a transport cannot become a second unchecked admission path. The submitted-answer and submission shapes carry NO `.optional()` — an optional field is exactly a field a producer can skip in silence. The generated instruction covers every declared field in BOTH directions and marks every mandatory one, so a field added to the registry cannot go silently unasked and the copied skeleton cannot teach a producer about a field that no longer exists. Every static arm runs against a violating fixture, plus two fixtures that must NOT fire (the gate copying the source; a comment describing the rule).

guards.name: redaction-surface-scan
guards.invariant: D183 (ref guards-and-tests §3.15): the 2j sweep proving no classified value reaches a wire, a durable row, a ledger file, a notification or a provider unreviewed. Two halves, neither sufficient alone. (a) The DECLARATION audit walks every registered surface's own schema through z.toJSONSchema and demands a declared ORIGIN — repository-authored, declared-redacted, local-filesystem-name, captured-hr-value, external-text — for every free-text and open-JSON leaf, then holds that origin against the surface's EGRESS class (operator-loopback, phone-scoped, durable-authority, durable-file, process-egress, os-notification). A redacted subtree is recognised structurally by its state/classification/transform arm signature, so an embedded `$ref` cannot decompose it back into a free-text key plus an open value; every other leaf is either provably closed (enum, literal, number, boolean, pattern/format-constrained string) or must be dispositioned. An advisory prompt may therefore carry ONLY what this repository wrote or explicitly redacted, an OS notification only repository-authored text, and durable free text needs a written exception naming the decision that admits it. Because the audit is driven off the schema, a field ADDED to a wire contract lands undispositioned and the guard goes red before it can ship; a new module under src/domain/dashboard, or a new exported *WireSchema no registered surface carries, fails the same way in both directions. A `*Redacted`-suffixed leaf must be declared `declared-redacted` or its NAME must be waived with a reason, and the producer half scans src/ for any `<name>Redacted:` write that is not a schema declaration. (b) The CANARY sweep plants ref clock-config-secrets §6's exact sentinel list — password, cookie, storage state, private key, credential-file path, an unissued SSN, an impossible DOB — plus a person name and an EID, asserts the plant reached the source, and then drives the REAL producers: buildFailureTriagePrompt over a maximal FailureRecord (nothing survives, and every dropped path still appears as a withheld fact), projectNotificationTrigger over all seven trigger arms plus a proof that every arm's schema REFUSES free text in every field, ledgerLineForOutbox (no universal canary, and an undeclared key cannot ride along), buildRunEvidenceReceipt over the real 2026-08-04 person-lookup exit run seeded into a real authority database (the subject's full name is present in the checkpoints and absent from the receipt, which still answers with its declared last4), and redactDiagnosticFields (an unclassified field is dropped WITH a warning). Every arm carries a negative control executed through the guard's own entry points: undispositioned leaf, refused origin, missing exception, gratuitous exception, stale disposition, orphan disposition, a decoy shape that merely resembles a redacted arm, a fixture producer writing urlRedacted/titleRedacted raw, and a positive control proving the canary scanner fires. It deliberately does not restate no-secret-values-in-logs, secrets-single-source, evidence-receipt, advisory-redaction, notification-durability or capture-durability-and-scope; it audits in one sweep the surfaces those guards each see one at a time.

guards.name: dashboard-refresh-boundary
guards.invariant: Ref frontend-backend-integration §8.14: every src/dashboard/surfaces/*.tsx and src/dashboard/app/*.tsx module exports React components only (uppercase-named functions, classes, or memo/forwardRef/lazy wrappers; type exports are erased and legal). Hooks, pure folds, vocabularies and object/array constants live in a sibling <surface>-model.ts. @vitejs/plugin-react accepts a module as a Fast Refresh boundary only when every export is a component or is reference-equal across re-evaluation, so one exported helper makes every edit to the surface invalidate upward into dashboard-app.tsx and remount the whole app. Both arms run against checked-in fixtures: one violating in every way the rule can break (hook, helper, object constant, array constant, lowercase re-export), one clean (declared, memo'd, forwardRef'd, arrow and re-exported components plus types). src/dashboard/ds/** is out of scope by design — ui.tsx is the one mixed barrel.

guards.name: command-result-exhaustive
guards.invariant: D253 (ref frontend-backend-integration §"D253"): every module under src/dashboard/** settles a CommandResult through the ONE exhaustive fold (src/dashboard/app/command-result.ts), never by testing one refusal arm and letting the other fall through. CommandResultSchema has three arms and TWO are refusals — `conflict` (the CAS refusal, carrying the server's currentVersion) and `rejected` (a kernel refusal code). A surface reading `state === "rejected"` alone treats a conflict as success: the Context rail's Data save closed its editor, discarded the operator's drafts and reported a correction SAVED that the kernel had refused on a version check, and the notification bell swallowed a stale-revision refusal in silence. Neither wrote a fallback; an unhandled union arm IS the fallback, and a false "submitted" on the surface whose job is explaining what happened is the exact failure the fail-loud rule exists to prevent. The guard scans every .ts/.tsx under src/dashboard and fails any module that names one refusal arm without the other; naming both in one condition is legal and clean, since that is exhaustive. Exempt: the fold itself (it is the thing being enforced) and src/dashboard/client/commands.ts, whose job is to PARSE the union rather than act on it. A negative control runs the walker against tests/unit/architecture/fixtures/command-result-unhandled-conflict.ts — the exact shipped shape — and against a clean both-arms condition, so a scan that resolved nothing cannot report the tree clean. Track D row D3 (2026-08-21) added the SECOND arm: "one arm without the other" is trivially satisfied by a module that names NEITHER — it posts a command, ignores the answer entirely, and every refusal lands on the success path in silence. All nine command-issuing surfaces now call the fold, so a module under src/dashboard/** that calls .executeCommand( must IMPORT src/dashboard/app/command-result.js. The IMPORT is what is checked rather than a mention of the function name, because a comment explaining the fold would otherwise clear the very module that ignores it (that is the first thing this arm caught); an imported-but-uncalled binding is refused by eslint --max-warnings 0. Its own negative control is tests/unit/architecture/fixtures/command-result-unfolded-dispatch.ts, plus a posts-and-folds string and a posts-nothing string that must both read clean.

guards.name: roadmap-doc-binding
guards.invariant: D263 (roadmap §Governance; ref guards-and-tests): the plan's two forms are bound to each other BOTH ways, mechanically. The prose in docs/rebuild/** is normative and the tree in docs/roadmap/roadmap.md is its machine-readable form and the operator's tracking view, so a rename on either side must fail this gate instead of rotting into two plans that disagree. Five arms, all decided by ONE pure function of (planText, files) so the real tree and every fixture go through identical code. (a) Every doc: ref on every node resolves: a phase ref (03a) names exactly one docs/rebuild/03a-*.md, a reference ref (ref:write-safety) names docs/rebuild/reference/write-safety.md, and a §section matches a heading's NUMBER (§5.4, §5 for '## 5. …'), its TEXT exactly (the phase docs number no headings, so §Phase summary is the only way to cite one) or, for a range (§14.1–14.2), both endpoints as numbers; a refusal names the file, the section and the headings it nearly matched, because 'no such section' alone is a sentence nobody can act on (D261). Headings inside fenced code are not headings. (b) Every <!-- roadmap: id --> tag and every <!-- roadmap-status: id --> block in docs/rebuild/** (minus the superseded history/ and reviews/ folders, skipped by NAME while that rename is in flight) and docs/migrations/** names a node the plan declares — asserted by CALLING the generator's own bindDocsToPlan rather than restating its rule, so the site and the gate can never refuse different things (D252), and by proving the guard's scan is byte-identical to scanDocs'. (c) Every non-phase node carries at least one doc: ref; a phase may omit one, because a phase is a container and its children carry the contracts. (d) Every node is described by at least one tagged doc section — a node no doc describes is a planning gap. (e) Every builds: line carries a layer tag; parsePlan refuses one that does not, and the arm is belt-and-braces over the parsed shape because a Feature may still be a bare string in the schema. Arms (c) and (d) ship as RATCHETS declared IN the test file: ALLOW_MISSING_DOC_REF lists the 59 nodes unbound at HEAD (the notation grew doc: on 2026-08-20 and only {#phase-0} was bound by the dogfood commit; cohesion-plan step 5.0 pastes the node map's doc: column onto the rest and step 6 empties the list) and ALLOW_UNTAGGED is EMPTY and must stay so, since step 3a's skeletons tagged all 66 nodes. A ratchet only shrinks: an allowlisted id whose gap has closed fails as stale, and one naming no node at all fails as a rename rather than a closed gap. Nine checked-in fixtures under tests/unit/architecture/fixtures/roadmap-binding/ are miniature repos with the same docs/ layout, read by the same collector as the repo: clean (every ref resolving — a heading by name, a numbered reference section, a range, a migrations tag, and a dangling tag under BOTH superseded folder names that must not be read), dangling-phase-doc, dangling-section (two refusals: no such heading, and a heading under a longer title), unknown-reference-slug, tag-names-no-node, status-names-no-node, node-without-doc-ref (which is then held by an explicit ratchet entry), node-with-no-tag and builds-without-layer. Each is asserted to fail with a message naming the ref, tag or id and its file, and the clean tree is asserted non-empty in both directions — a walker that resolved nothing would otherwise report every arm green.

guards.name: workflow-layout
guards.invariant: PLANNED by D265 (ref workflow-model §1.2.2, 2026-08-21): the `src/workflows/` tree IS the rail and the timeline, and the served role and the path are pinned to each other. (a) Every registered module's path matches its role's arm — `src/workflows/<id>/` for `standalone`/`composition` (a rail entry), `src/workflows/<of>/<step>/` for `chunk-harness` (a step of its composition), `src/workflows/proving/<id>/` for `proving` (test equipment, D220/D241) — and nothing else lives under `src/workflows/`; a stray folder is refused. (b) For every workflow that declares a D225 timeline, the declared categories and the step folders are the SAME set, both directions, each refusal naming the offender. (c) Every `chunk-harness.step` names one of `of`'s declared categories. (d) `descriptor-coverage` and `workflow-editor-compile-integrity` derive a descriptor's path from its ROLE, never from its id alone. Activates in the commit that moves `src/workflows/` into the D265 shape (doc 03b §The workflow tree — folders are the rail and the timeline), not before; a violating fixture per arm.
